from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: Wave Superposition", ["Light waves superimpose when they meet.", "This creates complex interference patterns.", "Imagine ripples in a quiet pond."])
        
        # Waves representation
        wave1 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).set_stroke(width=2)
        wave2 = Circle(radius=0.5, color=WHITE).set_stroke(width=2)
        
        self.place_at_grid(wave1, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(wave2, 'C5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.play(Create(wave1), Create(wave2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        wave1_anim = wave1.animate.scale(2).set_opacity(0.5)
        wave2_anim = wave2.animate.scale(2).set_opacity(0.5)
        self.play(wave1_anim, wave2_anim)
        
        # Interference zone
        interference = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.5 + i*0.2, color=GREY).set_stroke(width=1) for i in range(3)])
        self.place_in_area(interference, 'B3', 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(interference))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        constructive = Dot(color="#FF0000")
        destructive = Dot(color="#0000FF")
        self.place_at_grid(constructive, 'B4')
        self.place_at_grid(destructive, 'D4')
        self.play(FadeIn(constructive), FadeIn(destructive))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Photography only captures light intensity.", 
            "Holography records the wave phase.", 
            "It uses reference and object beams.", 
            "They interfere to create depth.", 
            "This reveals true three-dimensional images."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Holography: Encoding the Phase", lecture_lines)
        
        # Prepare elements
        ref_beam = Line(start=self.grid['A1'], end=self.grid['F1'], color="#FFFFFF")
        obj_beam = Line(start=self.grid['A3'], end=self.grid['F3'], color="#FFFFFF")
        plate = Rectangle(height=4, width=0.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(plate, 'C5')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.play(Create(ref_beam), Create(obj_beam))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF69B4")
        self.play(FadeIn(plate))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#7FFF00")
        fringe = VGroup(*[Line(plate.get_left(), plate.get_right(), color="#FFFFFF", stroke_width=2) for _ in range(10)])

        self.lecture[4].set_color("#FFA500")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Holograms act like diffraction gratings.",
            "Coherent light reconstructs original fronts.",
            "This projects images into space.",
            "The 3D scene appears reconstructed.",
            "Complex data becomes visible light."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Reconstruction: Decoding the 3D Image", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define objects
        hologram = Rectangle(width=2, height=3, color=BLUE).set_fill(BLUE, opacity=0.3)

        laser = Line(start=[-4, 0, 0], end=[-1, 0, 0], color=RED, stroke_width=4)
        
        reconstructed_wave = VGroup(*[Arc(radius=i*0.3, angle=PI/2, color=YELLOW) for i in range(1, 6)])
        self.place_at_grid(reconstructed_wave, 'C5')
        
        obj_3d = Sphere(radius=0.5, color=GREEN).set_fill(GREEN, opacity=0.7)
        self.place_at_grid(obj_3d, 'E5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(hologram), Create(laser))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===

        self.wait(1)

outline.topic: The Magic of Light: Principles of Diffraction and Holography

sections.title: Prerequisite: Wave Superposition
sections.content: Briefly introduce the principle of superposition: when two light waves meet, they create an interference pattern. Visual focus: overlapping ripples in a pond.
sections.example: Visualize two stones dropped into a pond simultaneously; the resulting complex pattern of crests and troughs is the foundation of holography.

sections.title: Diffraction: Light Bending Around Obstacles
sections.content: Define diffraction as the behavior of light waves bending around small apertures or edges. Introduce the concept of the 'diffraction pattern' as a fingerprint of an object.
sections.example: Shining a laser pointer through a tiny pinhole creates a central bright spot surrounded by concentric rings—the 'Airy disk'.

sections.title: Holography: Encoding the Phase
sections.content: Explain that photography only captures intensity (brightness), but holography captures phase (distance/depth) by using an interference pattern between a reference beam and a reflected object beam.
sections.example: A holographic 'security sticker' on a credit card: tilting it causes the light to diffract at different angles, revealing a 3D depth effect.

sections.title: Reconstruction: Decoding the 3D Image
sections.content: Describe how the interference pattern (hologram) acts like a complex diffraction grating. When coherent light hits it, it 'reconstructs' the original wave front.
sections.example: The 'Iron Man' holographic interface: a light source shines through the recorded diffraction pattern, projecting a 3D avatar of a character into mid-air.

sections.title: Summary and Real-world Application
sections.content: Synthesize the lesson: Holography is simply the recording of a diffraction pattern. Conclude with modern applications in medicine, data storage, and art.
sections.example: Mention holographic medical imaging, where doctors view a 3D scan of a heart floating in space, allowing for precise surgery planning.
